# Reading a message body by its declared type name

`{{messages.<type>.<field>}}` addresses one declared type. A node subscribing to
several types resolves each by name and never mixes them, and a body composed in
one frame is read the same way in the next.

## Two types on one node

```yaml
name: typed-message-demo
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: ops/alpha
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        a: {type: string}
      required: [a]
  - type: ops/beta
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        b: {type: string}
      required: [b]
nodes:
  - type: reactor
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/alpha
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
      - node: ops/beta
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          from_alpha:
            type: string
            source: '{{messages.ops/alpha.a | "none"}}'
          from_beta:
            type: string
            source: '{{messages.ops/beta.b | "none"}}'
```

Each directive carries a fallback literal.

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$BASE/v1/instances/$IID/messages" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"type":"ops/alpha","payload":{"a":"A1"}}'
```

In the frame `ops/alpha` opened, the node settles with:

```json
{"from_alpha": "A1", "from_beta": "none"}
```

Send `ops/beta` and, in the frame that opens, the same node settles with:

```json
{"from_alpha": "none", "from_beta": "B1"}
```

One node that could react to either type never confuses them.

## The type name is a real contract

```yaml
          v:
            type: string
            source: "{{messages.ops/alpha.nosuch}}"
```

Registration is refused with 400, naming the field. A misspelled name does not
become a silent empty value.

## Composing a body and carrying it to the next frame

```yaml
name: typed-message-carry
version: "1"
messages:
  - type: ops/carry
    body_schema:
      type: object
      properties:
        value: {type: integer}
      required: [value]
nodes:
  - type: counter
    kind: loop_counter
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          max:   {type: integer, default: 1}
          count: {type: integer}

  - type: sender
    sends_message: ops/carry
    subscribes:
      - node: counter
        type: attribute/count/changed
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          value: {type: integer, source: "{{nodes.counter.attribute.count}}"}
        required: [value]

  - type: later
    kind: attribute_passthrough
    subscribes:
      - node: ops/carry
        type: terminal/success
        force_upstream_refresh: false
    attributes:
      schema:
        type: object
        properties:
          carried: {type: integer, source: "{{messages.ops/carry.value}}"}
```

The sender composes the body from an attribute it holds and puts one message in
the ledger, attributed to the instance. That message opens the second of the
instance's two frames, and `later` runs in it, reading the value back through
the same grammar:

```json
{"carried": 1}
```

Message bodies are typed attribute blocks the author both writes and reads, with
one grammar for both directions.
